NOVEL-AND-FEASIBLE IDEATION:

STEP 1 — INVENT THE OBSERVABLE:
Standard practice tracks open-circuit voltage and seal leakage rate as direct indicators of failure. My observable is the **acoustic emission signature of microcrack formation**, specifically the high-frequency (>100 kHz) stress wave energy released during thermal cycling, which precedes visible cracks and voltage drop.

STEP 2 — MAKE THE IMPLEMENTATION BORING:
The observable is computable from standard piezoelectric acoustic emission sensors (already commonly used in structural health monitoring) with signal processing via fast Fourier transform and energy integration, using existing temperature and voltage data for correlation.

NOVELTY STATEMENT:
Standard practice tracks macroscopic failure indicators (voltage drop, leakage rate) that appear only after significant damage. My observable tracks the **microcrack formation energy** through acoustic emission analysis, which directly connects to the failure physics by quantifying the energy release from the differential expansion-induced cracking at the interfaces during thermal cycling. This provides early detection before catastrophic failure.

PHYSICS CHECK:
The governing physical relation is the elastic energy release rate during crack formation: G = E·ε²/(1-ν), where E is Young's modulus, ε is strain, and ν is Poisson's ratio. For YSZ (E=200 GPa, ν=0.3) with a thermal expansion mismatch of 10⁻⁶/°C over 775°C ΔT, strain ε = α·ΔT = 7.75×10⁻⁴. CALCULATED energy release rate G = 200e9·(7.75e-4)²/(1-0.3) = 1.71×10⁵ J/m³. This magnitude is detectable by acoustic emission sensors with thresholds of ~10⁻⁴ J.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
Components:
- 3 piezoelectric acoustic emission sensors (frequency range 100-1000 kHz, sensitivity >60 dB)
- Signal conditioning amplifier (bandpass filter 100-400 kHz)
- Data acquisition system (sampling rate ≥1 MHz, already part of existing monitoring)
- Signal processing software (standard FFT algorithm, energy integration routine)

Materials:
- High-temperature adhesive for sensor attachment (rated to 850°C)
- Ceramic waveguides (if needed for signal transmission)

Procedure:
1. Mount sensors at critical locations (seal interface, cathode-electrolyte boundary)
2. Record acoustic emission signals during thermal cycling
3. Filter and integrate signals to calculate stress wave energy
4. Correlate energy spikes with temperature cycles

All components are off-the-shelf; no new infrastructure required.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: ADDS minimal sensor mounting (comparable to existing thermocouple installation)
- Operability: NO change (existing logging system can capture additional data stream)
- Maintenance: ADDS periodic sensor inspection (similar to existing sensor maintenance)
- Cost class: MINOR increase (sensors and signal processing are commodity items)

Expected conclusion: NEGLIGIBLE additional deployment burden for significant early-warning benefit.

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol:
1. Subject modified stack to thermal cycling (25°C to 800°C at 5°C/min)
2. Monitor acoustic emission energy during each cycle
3. Record open-circuit voltage and seal leakage after each cycle

Pass/Fail Thresholds:
- PASS: Acoustic emission energy remains below 1×10⁻³ J/cycle for all 500 cycles
- PASS: Open-circuit voltage stays above 1.0 V after all cycles
- PASS: Seal leakage remains below 1% of fuel flow after all cycles

Duration: 500 complete thermal cycles (approximately 83 hours at 5°C/min ramp rate)

Kill Criterion: Test fails immediately if:
- Acoustic emission energy exceeds 1×10⁻³ J/cycle in any 3 consecutive cycles
- Open-circuit voltage drops below 1.0 V at any point
- Seal leakage exceeds 1% of fuel flow at any point
- Stack mass increases by more than 2% at any point
